outcomes: Checks whether the centre pawn is already under pressure before asking a pinning bishop a question
Plays or declines the question in an unlabeled opening position, with the centre check as the reason
Recognises a position with no pin, where there is nothing to ask
sources: docs/lessons-openings.md (weaknesses section) and content/skills/POS.PIN.STRATEGIC.json (conditions from the Nimzowitsch sheet, ideas only, original wording)

items: IBds57-1..6 and IBds57-32 (authored, engine-checked at recorded depth; the failing board differs by two changes and the cause of its loss is not claimed), shipped items are drawn by the practice step

steps.text: You know the four policies from *A pin can last: four ways to meet it*. Here you decide, from a bare position, whether to ask. Check one thing first: **can the centre open?** As a *rule of thumb*, if your centre pawn (here d5) is already pressed, by a pawn or by a pawn and pieces, it can. Then the bishop may come back to life.

The question is a *rule of thumb*, not a law. It works best when the centre stays shut: the driven bishop finds few squares and cannot return. It fails when the centre can open, or when no pin exists, because then there is nothing to ask. Often several moves are sound, so asking is one option, not a duty.

steps.title: Same question, three boards
steps.prompt: Board 1: no White pawn attacks d5. Is ...h6 sound? Board 2: two changes, a pawn on c4 and a knight on c3, so d5 is attacked twice. Does the question still hold? Board 3: the bishop is still on c1. Is there anything to ask? Predict each, then check.
For each silent position, did you check whether a pawn attacks the centre before you chose? In which position did that check change your move?

steps.text: **Remember.** Asking a pinning bishop a question, such as ...h6, is a rule of thumb, not a duty. First check whether the centre can open: is your centre pawn already pressed? If it can open, the bishop may come back to life. If no pin exists, there is nothing to ask. Often several moves are sound.
